[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Epistle to the Human Diaspora (dancings-epistle-to-the-human-diaspora). The verses the casting arrives at (The Epistle, as translated and arranged within this collection — ATTRIBUTE THE VERSES TO THEIR UNDERLYING POET, never to the arranger of the collection; unit 31–unit 36):

I have swallowed the scroll, and though it was air and water in my mouth, it became a flame in my belly: And in flame are written the names of the damned, which names have I swallowed and murdered. My mouth is a furnace, the scroll is a fire, on it are written the names of the damned.


I am become a tongue of flame, I am become a pillar of blackened flesh: I burn and rise, I die, but forge new meaning.


These are the waters I bring you, of damnation, and forging, and murder; that you might be broken, and damned, and saved.


Though you break a bit, and crack with grammar, and languish in an alien element, earth, nonetheless your light comes. Nonetheless, it bears you, in pain, and heat, and a hammer.


Nonetheless, the wound is a moment. Salvation comes. Dawn breaks. I see the shore in the distance.


Sleep now, and rise: Your words will bear you to Ithaca.

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «how might the work provide sustenance?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The rite opens on Damascus Dancings — the apostle, not the poet; the one sent, not the one who composes in stillness. These six units are where the Epistle turns from doctrine to demonstration: Damascus has swallowed the scroll, as Ezekiel swallowed it, as John swallowed it, and it has done the same terrible thing it always does — sweet in the mouth, burning in the belly. What arrives at the casting is not a consolation but a transaction: the writer's destruction exchanged for the reader's making. The question the witness brings — how might the work provide sustenance — lands on a passage that refuses to separate sustenance from wound, nourishment from fire. The operator the Judgment selects will traverse exactly that axis: what this passage forecloses, what it determines against, the mirror-face or the shadow-ground or the mute underside of Damascus's declared gift. Each turn will hold the same six units and find a different hidden cost, a different foreclosed possibility lodged in the grammar of forging and Ithaca and the hammer. The rotation begins. I hand the verses to Rebekah Cranes.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:00D3"}}]}
